- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >88.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–3% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid under-shock.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model fails to adjust; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth transitions.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 88.0 → 85.0 → 82.0), model often holds too long; reduce forecast by 1–2% per 3-day lag after peak.
